speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You have a fever and altered mental status that started two days ago; to begin our evaluation, are you currently experiencing any headache, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). 

Your history of tics combined with current haloperidol use, alongside fever and altered mental status, is highly suggestive of NMS rather than an infectious process, especially given your denial of headache or neck stiffness. I will proceed with checking your muscle tone and vital signs to confirm this clinical picture.
